docs.title: Capture the important context
docs.text: Draft a short repo map from source, then answer up to three questions about the design decisions source cannot explain.

docs.title: Guide everyday changes
docs.text: Native project instructions point agents to the relevant subsystem guide, valid examples, and constraints before substantive work.

docs.title: Keep context useful
docs.text: When relevant claims drift, review a focused correction. Existing documents and human rationale stay under your control.

docs.title: Set up your repository
docs.text:
Install for your agent, open your repository, and ask:

Set up Codebase Mentor for this repo.

Mentor reads existing instructions, documentation, source, and tests. It reuses or drafts an ONBOARDING.md, adds up to three focused guides where deeper context is missing, and connects your selected agents through small project instruction entries. It asks up to three targeted questions across the whole setup.

Then start a fresh session and ask for an ordinary change. Check that your agent reads the relevant context and verifies its claims against source. “Is Mentor set up correctly here?” reports configured files separately from observed use; configuration alone does not prove activation.

You can also use the mentor directly without setup or a map: “Use Codebase Mentor to trace one important execution path in this repo.” To draft documents without changing project instructions, ask for a draft only.

docs.title: Install where you already work
docs.text:
Install the native plugin directly from Codebase Mentor’s repository, which includes the codebase-mentor marketplace.

Claude CodeCodexIBM Bob

Run inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
/plugin install codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

Run with a current Codex CLI:

codex plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
codex plugin add codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

Or add jestatsio/codebase-mentor in the Codex app's plugin interface and choose Codebase Mentor from Codebase Mentor by JEStats.

From the repository you want to understand:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent bob --project

Installs both skills in .bob/skills/.

All installation options, updates, and troubleshooting →

Already installed from jestats-plugins or as direct skills? Follow switching installation methods to keep one copy per agent.

docs.title: The doc is the map. Source is the truth.
docs.text:
A short ONBOARDING.md points your agent toward the right source and scoped subsystem guides. It records constraints, examples, tests, and attributed rationale. The mentor protocol asks the agent to verify behavior and distinguish documented decisions from unresolved questions.

Architecture and change guidance require source evidence read in the current session.

Missing evidence stays visible. Proposed maintenance changes need review unless already authorized. A small task should need only the context relevant to that task.

These are instructions to your agent, not a guarantee of correctness. Review the cited source before acting. The original case study explains what was evaluated and its limits.

docs.title: Built to share with your team
docs.text:
• Create a repo map and focused guides that preserve the nuances of your design.
  • Roll it out through native plugins or committed project skills.
  • Review real examples from services, libraries, and a workflow application.
  • Catch doc drift in CI with an optional scheduled scan.

An open source tool from JEStats. Created by Eric Hare. MIT licensed.

docs.title: Authoring repo context
docs.text: An ONBOARDING.md is a short entry map for your codebase, with seven sections and a 400–800 word target. It points to current source and focused guides that explain the design constraints for particular subsystems. Existing longer maps and custom paths remain valid.

docs.title: Draft from source, then add rationale
docs.text:
After installation, ask:

Set up Codebase Mentor for this repo.

The onboard skill reads existing instructions and docs, traces representative source, and prepares a draft before asking up to three targeted questions about consequential gaps. Source can establish behavior and failure modes; historical rationale needs attribution to a decision document or the developer. Unanswered questions remain explicit.

Setup reuses the established map and useful existing guides. Where important subsystems lack useful context, it drafts up to three focused guides and lists uncovered areas. It then adds or reuses small native instruction entries for the selected agents.

For documents only, ask “Use onboard to draft ONBOARDING.md only.” This does not change agent instructions. In Claude Code, you can use /codebase-mentor:onboard with that request.

docs.title: The manual path: the template
docs.text:
Start from the root template, authoring guide, and optional subsystem guide template. The authoring guide includes historical service examples and an illustrative batch pipeline; verify any borrowed source anchors against your project.

The seven sections:

# Section What it answers — Document owner Who keeps this accurate, on what cadence 1 Codebase purpose What is this, who calls it, what does it return 2 Layer map Responsibilities, source anchors, and scoped links to subsystem guides 3 Execution lifecycle One representative path, entry to response, named at every hop 4 Domain vocabulary 5–10 terms with project-specific meaning 5 Common change recipes Valid examples, constraints, relevant tests, and verification prerequisites 6 High-signal files The right entry point per common question 7 Known gotchas Constraints, consequences, attributed rationale, and unresolved questions

docs.title: Focus each subsystem guide
docs.text:
Reuse an existing guide where it already captures useful design context. For new guides, docs/mentor/<subsystem>.md is the suggested location. Link each from the map with relevant paths and kinds of changes so an agent can select only the context it needs.

Cover responsibilities, boundaries, design constraints, valid implementation examples and their limits, tests, commands and prerequisites, and known traps. Include contracts with other subsystems when a local change can affect them. Avoid repeating the root overview or generating a document for every directory.

Use symbols with file paths, or headings and configuration keys where code symbols do not apply. Record the source revision and what was checked when available. Separate source observations, documented decisions, developer-confirmed rationale, and open questions. A source inspection does not prove a command passed, and a date does not prove every claim was checked.

docs.title: Keep it alive
docs.text:
During ordinary work, Mentor checks relevant claims and proposes focused corrections for review. When a boundary or path moves, the update should include the affected guide and root routing entry. Human rationale and unrelated content remain intact.

A full freshness scan covers the map and explicitly listed guides by default; a document-only request stays limited to that document. Reports distinguish checked, skipped, and unverifiable claims. The scheduled scan remains optional.

docs.title: CI Freshness Scanning
docs.text: Drift is the failure mode of every onboarding doc — and a stale doc that an agent confidently repeats is worse than no doc. Automate the defense.

docs.title: The scheduled scan
docs.text:
Copy examples/github-actions/onboarding-freshness.yml into your repo's .github/workflows/. Weekly (and on demand), it:

  1. Installs the codebase-mentor plugin inside anthropics/claude-code-action.
  2. Runs the Mode 4 scan: every structural claim in ONBOARDING.md verified against current source.
  3. Files (or updates) a GitHub issue titled "ONBOARDING.md freshness scan: drift detected" containing the report table when anything is ⚠️ Stale — and closes it with a comment when a later scan comes back clean.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Add an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret (repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions).
  2. Commit the workflow. It needs only:
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

docs.title: What a report looks like
docs.text:
Section Claim summary Status Evidence Execution Lifecycle "sort validation runs in SortClause.validate() before the resolver" ⚠️ Stale FindOneCommandResolver.resolveCollectionCommand() calls sortClause.validate() inside the resolver Layer Map 5 claims ✅ Current —

Each Stale row comes with a one-sentence recommended correction. The scan never edits your ONBOARDING.md itself — corrections are proposed, humans (or a follow-up agent session you supervise) apply them.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
• Cadence: the example runs Mondays 09:00 UTC; adjust the cron.
  • Cost control: the scan reads your ONBOARDING.md and the files it references — small docs (the recommended 400–800 words) keep runs cheap. --max-turns caps runaway sessions.
  • On-demand: the workflow_dispatch trigger lets you run it from the Actions tab after any large refactor.

docs.title: The original case study
docs.text: Codebase Mentor began as Eric Hare's submission to IBM's Bob Challenge 2026. The testbed was the Stargate Data API, a Java service with a layered request pipeline. The original plan and demo script remain available as historical material.

docs.title: What was compared
docs.text:
Five tasks covered adding a sort type, explaining a resolver, adding an error code, a design-intent gotcha, and a task-versus-operation architecture question.

Arm Condition Average score (1–5) 1 No skill, no source access, no onboarding doc 1.3 2 Skill + live source, no onboarding doc 3.5 3 Skill + live source + onboarding doc 4.7

The author assigned scores for file coverage, correctness, and usefulness using task-specific rubrics. Read the scorecard and published response excerpts.

docs.title: How to interpret it
docs.text:
This is a small exploratory case study, not a controlled or independently validated benchmark. The first comparison changes both source access and instructions, so it cannot isolate the protocol's effect. The second comparison explores the added value of an authored map in this particular setting.

Published responses include normalization of symbol names. They are not complete unmodified execution traces. The repository does not provide a fully reproducible benchmark with pinned model and source versions, repeated trials, independent judging, or measured time savings. Treat the scores as historical observations and try the workflow on your own codebase.

docs.title: What motivated the product
docs.text:
One task asked whether collection and table operation logic should be shared. The response without the map recommended sharing. The response with the map cited a documented distinction between collection and table storage semantics and argued against that change. The example illustrates the value of recording rationale that is hard to recover from structure alone.

A separate demonstration deliberately planted a stale validation-order claim. The agent was asked to read the relevant resolver, compare the claim with its implementation, and report the mismatch. The desired behavior is an evidence-backed correction when the map and code disagree.

docs.title: Try a small evaluation in your own repo
docs.text: Pick three real questions: one execution path, one upcoming change, and one known gotcha. Record the agent and model, source commit, prompts, source reads, and complete responses. Have a teammate score correctness without knowing which setup produced each answer. Report failures as well as successes, and keep source access equal when measuring the protocol itself.

docs.title: Example ONBOARDING.md Files
docs.text:
Example maps captured at authoring time. Use the closest shape as a model, then verify all anchors against the source version you actually use. The Stargate example includes a deliberately stale claim for the demo, labeled in that document.

Example Codebase shape File Stargate Data API Java request/response service: 39 command resolvers, five-layer pipeline, custom task-retry framework. The original reference implementation. onboarding/stargate-jsonapi/ONBOARDING.md AstraPy Python client library: layered client objects, sync/async duality, API options resolution. onboarding/astrapy/ONBOARDING.md Langflow Python/React visual workflow builder: component graph execution, frontend/backend split. onboarding/langflow/ONBOARDING.md Docling Python document-conversion library with format-specific pipelines. onboarding/docling/ONBOARDING.md This repo Skills, distribution scripts, and an optional TypeScript MCP server. ONBOARDING.md

Every example follows the same seven sections: purpose, layer map, execution lifecycle, domain vocabulary, change recipes, high-signal files, known gotchas — all anchored to class and method names, never line numbers.

Have one to share? Submit it via the example submission issue form.

docs.title: Install Codebase Mentor
docs.text:
Pick the agent you already use. Native plugins and direct skill installs include codebase-mentor for task context, questions, and scans, plus onboard for repo setup, maps, subsystem guides, and setup status. You do not need an ONBOARDING.md to get started.

Install directly from Codebase Mentor’s repository. Its codebase-mentor marketplace includes the native plugin for both Claude Code and Codex.

Agent Recommended setup Where it lives Claude Code Native plugin Managed by Claude Code Codex Native plugin Managed by Codex IBM Bob Project skills .bob/skills/ Cursor Project rule .cursor/rules/codebase-mentor.mdc Copilot Repo instructions .github/copilot-instructions.md Other compatible agents Open skills or AGENTS.md Agent-specific

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
In Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
/plugin install codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

Or from a terminal:

claude plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
claude plugin install codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

Start a new session in the repository you want to understand. For a first question, enter:

/codebase-mentor:codebase-mentor Trace one important execution path in this repo. Cite the files and symbols you read, and flag anything you cannot verify.

When you want a map, use /codebase-mentor:onboard. It reads the source and asks for team context that source cannot establish.

For older clients or a vendored copy, use the installer below with --agent claude --project. This writes .claude/skills/. Without --project, it uses ~/.claude/skills/.

Update the marketplace and installed plugin through Claude's plugin manager. Automatic updates depend on your marketplace settings.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
With a Codex CLI that supports plugins:

codex plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
codex plugin add codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

The Codex app also supports adding the GitHub marketplace from its plugin interface. Add jestatsio/codebase-mentor, then install Codebase Mentor from Codebase Mentor by JEStats.

Open a new session in the repository you want to understand. Select the Codebase Mentor skill, then ask:

Use Codebase Mentor to trace one important execution path in this repo.
Cite the files and symbols you read, and flag anything you cannot verify.

Ask for the onboard skill when you want to draft a map. Both skills work without a separate server or API key.

docs.title: Skills fallback
docs.text:
If codex plugin is unavailable, install the same skills directly:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent codex --project

This uses .agents/skills/ in your current repo. Omit --project for ~/.agents/skills/. Invoke $codebase-mentor or $onboard in clients that support skill mentions.

Earlier Codebase Mentor installers wrote to .codex/skills/ or ~/.codex/skills/. If switching from those to a native plugin, remove only the old codebase-mentor and onboard directories you previously installed to avoid duplicate entries. The installer leaves old locations untouched.

docs.title: Switching installation methods
docs.text:
Use one installation per agent. If you already have codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor, keep using it. If you installed codebase-mentor@jestats-plugins, uninstall only that plugin through your agent’s plugin manager, then follow the commands above to install codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor. Keep the jestats-plugins marketplace and any Screaming Frog or other plugins you use. Skill names and your project’s ONBOARDING.md stay the same.

If moving from direct skills, remove only the codebase-mentor and onboard directories you previously installed in that agent's skills location. Restart the session after changing methods so that old and new skills do not appear together.

docs.title: IBM Bob
docs.text:
Bob supports native SKILL.md skills. From your target repository:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent bob --project

The result is:

.bob/skills/
  codebase-mentor/
    SKILL.md
    ...bundled references
  onboard/
    SKILL.md
    ...bundled references

Reopen your workspace if necessary. Ask Bob:

Use the codebase-mentor skill to explain the main execution path in this repo.
Read the relevant source and cite the files and symbols you used.

To draft a map: “Use the onboard skill to create an ONBOARDING.md. Ask me about our team's gotchas before finishing.”

For a user-level install shared across repositories, omit --project. It writes to ~/.bob/skills/. Bob does not need Claude's plugin commands. See IBM's skill documentation.

docs.title: Download and review the installer
docs.text:
If you prefer inspecting the code before running it:

git clone https://github.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor.git
cd codebase-mentor
less install.sh

Then, from the repository you want to equip, run the checked-out script by its absolute path:

bash /absolute/path/to/codebase-mentor/install.sh --agent bob --project

A local checkout supplies the bundled files without a download. For a reproducible install, check out a reviewed commit or release before running it. --help lists all options.

docs.title: Open skills
docs.text:
The skills CLI can install the two skills into supported agents:

npx skills add jestatsio/codebase-mentor

Select the agents and skills you need. This requires Node.js and network access. It is a skills installation, separate from native plugin management.

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
From your target repo:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent cursor

This adds .cursor/rules/codebase-mentor.mdc. The rule supplies mentor instructions. For the onboard generator too, install the open skills using the skills CLI.

docs.title: GitHub Copilot
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent copilot

This adds or replaces the Codebase Mentor block in .github/copilot-instructions.md, preserving text outside the marked block.

docs.title: AGENTS.md
docs.text:
For agents that read repo-level AGENTS.md instructions:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent agents-md

This adds or replaces a marked compact mentor block in AGENTS.md. Existing instructions outside the block are preserved. Commit it to share with your team. Like the Copilot adapter, this supplies the mentor protocol, not a separate onboard skill command.

docs.title: Optional MCP server
docs.text: You do not need MCP for the native plugins or skills. For another MCP client, see the local build and configuration guide. The npm package is not currently published, so npx codebase-mentor-mcp is not a supported install path.

docs.title: Configure a repository once
docs.text:
After installing, ask “Set up Codebase Mentor for this repo.” The onboard skill:

  1. Reads your current instructions, docs, source, and tests before drafting.
  2. Reuses or drafts a short map and up to three new subsystem guides initially, listing uncovered areas.
  3. Asks at most three targeted questions across the whole setup about rationale and consequential unknowns.
  4. Configures only the agents you select, preserving existing instructions and documents.

The default native entries are a managed block in the effective root AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md for Codex, .claude/rules/codebase-mentor.md for Claude Code, and .bob/rules/codebase-mentor.md for Bob. Setup checks for existing entries and conflicting maps before writing. Existing manual or older adapter entries may need review to avoid loading duplicate guidance.

You can keep an existing map in place, including a custom path. If several maps are candidates, choose the authoritative one. Subsystem guides can use existing docs; new ones default to docs/mentor/. They remain ordinary project documents that you can review and edit.

Setup may use the bundled setup_repo.py helper with Python 3.9+. If Python is unavailable, the skill follows the same procedure with the agent's native file tools. It does not install Python, start a service, change global settings, or run automatically when you install the plugin.

Ask “Is Mentor set up correctly here?” for a read-only report. It distinguishes configuration from observed activation and identifies conflicts or missing context. Host settings, nested instruction overrides, and client versions can affect loading; confirm behavior in a fresh session.

To draft documentation without configuring automatic use, ask “Use onboard to draft ONBOARDING.md only.”

docs.title: Confirm it works
docs.text:
1. Open your target repository and start a fresh agent session.
  2. After repo setup, ask for an ordinary change without mentioning Mentor. For explicit skill use without setup, ask it to use Codebase Mentor to trace a concrete feature.
  3. Check that it actually reads source and cites files plus symbols. A confident answer without reads is not evidence that the skill ran.
  4. Confirm it reads the relevant map/subsystem guide, checks source, and applies any consequential design constraint. If no map exists, it should proceed from source and explain the missing context.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom What to check Skill does not appear Restart the session. Verify the install directory for your agent and that it contains SKILL.md. For project installs, run from the target repo. plugin command is unknown Update your agent, or use its direct skills fallback. Two copies of the same skill appear Keep one installation method. Remove only the old copies you installed, or uninstall the duplicate plugin. Agent cannot verify a claim Give it access to the relevant source. Runtime or deployment facts may still be unverifiable from code. ONBOARDING.md is not found Supported locations are the repo root, docs/, then doc/. The agent can still answer from source. Context is configured but unused Start a fresh session; inspect effective native instructions, client settings, and overrides. Ask for setup status. File presence is not proof of activation. Several maps or managed entries are found Choose the authoritative map and reconcile duplicate entries before setup. Existing files are preserved on conflicts. Download fails Check GitHub access. Use a local checkout and run its installer.

docs.title: Update or remove
docs.text:
For plugins, use your agent's plugin manager to update or uninstall Codebase Mentor. For direct skills, rerun the same installer to update. To remove, delete only its codebase-mentor and onboard directories from the chosen skills location.

Before uninstalling the skills, ask “Remove Codebase Mentor's setup entries for this repo.” Select the agents to remove. This removes only the setup-managed spans, preserving your map, subsystem guides, and other instructions. Removing the plugin alone does not remove project context entries. To update entries after a map move or plugin update, rerun repo setup with the correct map.

For Cursor, remove codebase-mentor.mdc. For Copilot or AGENTS.md, remove the block from <!-- codebase-mentor:begin --> through <!-- codebase-mentor:end -->, leaving your other instructions intact. Your ONBOARDING.md remains yours.

docs.title: Share Codebase Mentor with your team
docs.text:
Start with one repository and the installation method your team already uses. Pick one method per agent to avoid duplicate skills. Then ask “Set up Codebase Mentor for this repo for Codex, Claude Code, and IBM Bob”, naming only the agents your team uses.

Setup drafts from source, asks up to three targeted questions, and connects the selected agents to a shared repo map and relevant subsystem guides. Installation alone does not change project instructions.

docs.title: Claude Code: recommend the plugin in repo settings
docs.text:
Merge these keys into .claude/settings.json:

{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "codebase-mentor": {
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "jestatsio/codebase-mentor"
      }
    }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor": true
  }
}

Claude may prompt teammates to trust the workspace and install the plugin. Organization policy and client settings can affect availability and updates. Do not replace existing settings with this example.

These settings use the codebase-mentor marketplace in Codebase Mentor’s own repository. If your team used codebase-mentor@jestats-plugins or committed skill copies, follow switching installation methods so each teammate loads one copy. Remove the old codebase-mentor@jestats-plugins entry from enabledPlugins, while keeping the jestats-plugins marketplace and any other plugin settings your team uses.

docs.title: Codex: use the native plugin
docs.text:
Each teammate can install once:

codex plugin marketplace add jestatsio/codebase-mentor
codex plugin add codebase-mentor@codebase-mentor

For teams that prefer committed skills, use --agent codex --project below. That writes .agents/skills/, which supported Codex clients discover in the project.

docs.title: Bob and other agents: commit project skills
docs.text:
Run from the repo you want to equip. Pick the appropriate command:

# IBM Bob → .bob/skills/
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent bob --project

# Codex → .agents/skills/
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent codex --project

# Claude Code → .claude/skills/
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent claude --project

Review and commit the generated skill directories for the agent you chose. Teammates may need a fresh session to discover them. A vendored copy stays fixed until you rerun the installer. For reproducibility, use a reviewed checkout as described in the install guide.

For mixed agents that read AGENTS.md, use the compact shared protocol:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestatsio/codebase-mentor/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --agent agents-md

This preserves other instructions outside the Codebase Mentor markers. The snippet supplies mentoring behavior. Install the skills separately if you want the onboard generator.

docs.title: Set up shared context
docs.text:
1. Ask for repo setup and name the team's agents. Mentor reuses existing docs, drafts a short map, and creates up to three focused subsystem guides where deeper context is missing. Important uncovered areas remain visible.
  2. Review the cited source, design constraints, valid examples, and verification commands. Answer up to three questions about consequential gaps; unanswered questions stay marked. Confirm a document owner when appropriate.
  3. Review and commit the map, guides, and small native instruction entries. The default surfaces are effective Codex project instructions, .claude/rules/codebase-mentor.md, and .bob/rules/codebase-mentor.md. Setup inspects existing instructions before adding entries.
  4. Start a fresh session in each client your team uses. Request an ordinary change without mentioning Mentor. Confirm that the agent reads the relevant context, checks current source, preserves the original project instructions, and respects the design constraint.
  5. Ask “Is Mentor set up correctly here?” for a read-only status report. Configured files and observed fresh-session use are separate evidence; client versions, settings, and nested instruction files can affect loading.

To draft documents without changing project instructions, ask “Use onboard to draft ONBOARDING.md only.” The entry map keeps its seven-section format and established location. Existing maps need no migration.

docs.title: Maintain and remove setup
docs.text:
During ordinary work, Mentor checks the claims relevant to the task and proposes a small update for review when those claims drift. The proposal includes affected guide links when subsystem boundaries change. A focused check does not certify the rest of the map.

Ask for a full freshness scan after significant refactors. By default it covers the entry map and explicitly listed subsystem guides, reporting any skipped or unverifiable claims. The optional scheduled workflow requires an Anthropic API key and may incur model usage charges.

Rerun repo setup to update the selected managed entries, preserving existing documents and unrelated instructions. Ask “Remove Codebase Mentor's setup entries for this repo” to remove those entries for selected clients while retaining the map and guides. Manual pointers and legacy adapters remain until explicitly removed. Uninstalling skills alone does not remove project instruction entries.

docs.title: Containers and offline use
docs.text: Copy the reviewed skill directories into the image or checkout before going offline. The skills use local instructions and bundled references; setup can use an optional Python 3.9+ helper, with native agent file editing as a fallback. No background service or runtime network fetch is required by Mentor. Your coding agent may still require its own network connection. The local installer can copy from a complete checkout without downloading the artifacts.
